newsitem.title: CANADA: DBRS confirms Newfoundland debt ratings.
newsitem.headline: DBRS confirms Newfoundland debt ratings.

text.p: Dominion Bond Rating Service said on Friday it confirmed the Province of Newfoundland's long-term debt at BBB(low) and short-term debt at R-2(middle), both with stable trends.
The government is consistently working to live within its means in the face of a weakening economy, DBRS said.
The province's fiscal program is expected to result in a C$7.0 million DBRS-adjusted surplus for the 1997-98 budget year, 0.1 percent of GDP, compared to a C$6.0 million deficit the year before.
Major fiscal adjustments have been necessary as lower revenues have required offsetting reductions in spending, DBRS said.
Despite stabilizing debt levels, the ratio of debt (tax-supported and unfunded pension liabilities) to GDP remains the highest of all provinces.
Debt to GDP is expected to reach 85 percent at the end of fiscal 1997-98 as further contraction of the economy is forecast for 1997.
Newfoundland's economy is in recession due to major restructuring in the natural resource, fishing and government sectors, and is projected to contract 2.7 percent in real terms.
